# Syntax Sprint: Pointers
<!-- Slide 39 -->

## Programming Activity

Create a simple program that declares:

- Two `int` variables and one pointer to an `int`
- Two `string` variables and one pointer to a `string`

Using **the pointer variables only**, display:

- The address held in the pointer
- The contents of each of the two variables

::: notes
Slides 39–40

Students must point each pointer at one variable, display through it, then reseat it to the second variable and display again. Watch for students who print `first` directly instead of `*intPtr`, or who forget `#include <string>`.

Solution in `cpp/syntax_sprint_pointers.cpp`:

```cpp
int first = 10;
int second = 20;
int* intPtr = &first;
cout << "intPtr holds " << intPtr << ", which contains " << *intPtr << "\n";
intPtr = &second;
cout << "intPtr holds " << intPtr << ", which contains " << *intPtr << "\n";

string course = "CISP 360";
string topic = "Pointers";
string* stringPtr = &course;
cout << "stringPtr holds " << stringPtr << ", which contains " << *stringPtr << "\n";
stringPtr = &topic;
cout << "stringPtr holds " << stringPtr << ", which contains " << *stringPtr << "\n";
```

Addresses differ from run to run; the values print as 10, 20, CISP 360, and Pointers.
:::
